method: OPEN AND QUOTED, from the RCH Melbourne Clinical Practice Guideline 'von Willebrand disease' (Last Updated April 2026), retrieved 2026-09-23. Every pass claim is machine re-checkable. claims.claim: ⚠️ **Discuss every child with VWD and bleeding with the paediatric haematology team**; plan treatment with a haematologist **before any procedure**.
claims.source_text: All children with von Willebrand disease (VWD) and bleeding should be discussed with the paediatric haematology team … A treatment plan should be made, in consultation with a haematologist, before performing any procedure
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'von Willebrand disease' (Last Updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/von_Willebrand_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **VWD is the most common inherited bleeding disorder**, affecting males and females equally: easy bruising, mucosal bleeding (epistaxis, oral mucosa, menorrhagia) and post-operative bleeding.
claims.source_text: Von Willebrand disease is the most common inherited bleeding disorder … Affects males and females equally Characterised by easy bruising, bleeding from mucous membranes (particularly epistaxis, oral mucosa, menorrhagia) and post-op bleeding
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'von Willebrand disease' (Last Updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/von_Willebrand_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Type 1 (common):** reduced VWF, mild bleeding. **Type 2 (uncommon):** abnormal VWF, variable bleeding. **Type 3 (rare):** near-absent VWF — may bleed like moderate–severe haemophilia, into joints and muscles.
claims.source_text: Type 1 (common) Reduced levels of VWF Typically associated with mild bleeding Type 2 (uncommon) Abnormal structure and function of VWF, several variants Variable bleeding pattern Type 3 (rare) Near absence of VWF Child may behave like those with moderate to severe haemophilia and experience joint/muscle bleeding.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'von Willebrand disease' (Last Updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/von_Willebrand_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Major haemorrhage, head injury or any suspected internal bleeding: give clotting factor immediately**, before a full assessment is complete.
claims.source_text: Major haemorrhage, head injury or any suspected internal bleeding should be treated with clotting factor immediately, before a full assessment is complete
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'von Willebrand disease' (Last Updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/von_Willebrand_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Establish** the site and extent of bleeding, the VWD type and severity, and any home treatment (e.g. tranexamic acid).
claims.source_text: Elicit a detailed description of site and extent of bleeding Determine type and severity of VWD (if known) Check if any type of treatment has been given at home eg tranexamic acid
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'von Willebrand disease' (Last Updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/von_Willebrand_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Routine coagulation studies are not required.** Consider FBE and ferritin after recurrent mucosal bleeding — anaemia and iron deficiency are common.
claims.source_text: Consider FBE and ferritin in children with a history of recurrent mucosal bleeding, as anaemia and iron deficiency are common … Routine coagulation studies are not required
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'von Willebrand disease' (Last Updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/von_Willebrand_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Tranexamic acid treats and prevents recurrence of mouth bleeds and epistaxis in all severities of VWD**, alone or with desmopressin or factor concentrate; often helpful for heavy menstrual bleeding.
claims.source_text: Effective for treating, and preventing the recurrence of, mouth bleeds and epistaxis in all severities of VWD May be given alone or as adjunct therapy to desmopressin or factor concentrate … Often helpful for management of heavy menstrual bleeding either as a primary treatment or in combination with hormonal management
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'von Willebrand disease' (Last Updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/von_Willebrand_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'von Willebrand disease' (Last Updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/von_Willebrand_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Dose: tranexamic acid 25 mg/kg/dose (max 1.5 g/dose) orally three times daily for 5–10 days**, depending on severity.
claims.source_text: Dose: Tranexamic acid (500 mg tablet) oral, 25 mg/kg/dose (max 1.5 g/dose) three times daily, for 5-10 days (duration dependent on severity of injury)
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'von Willebrand disease' (Last Updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/von_Willebrand_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Desmopressin is for mild–moderate Type 1 VWD with a documented safe and satisfactory desmopressin challenge.** Occasionally effective in Type 2, **never in Type 3**, and **not adequate alone for major bleeding.**
claims.source_text: Used in children with mild to moderate Type 1 VWD where there is a documented record of safe and satisfactory response to a desmopressin challenge Occasionally effective in Type 2 VWD, never effective in Type 3 VWD Not adequate as a single agent to achieve haemostasis in major bleeding
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'von Willebrand disease' (Last Updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/von_Willebrand_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Generally not used under 3 years or with seizure disorders** — it can cause hyponatraemia and seizures. **Fluid-restrict to about 2/3 of maintenance for 24 hours afterwards.**
claims.source_text: Generally, it is not used in children <3 years old or children with seizure disorders (can cause hyponatraemia and seizures) … Fluid restriction (approximately 2/3 of daily maintenance fluid requirement) is recommended for 24 hours following desmopressin administration
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'von Willebrand disease' (Last Updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/von_Willebrand_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Dose: desmopressin 0.3 microgram/kg (max 20 micrograms) once, IV or subcut.** IV: dilute to 50 mL with 0.9% sodium chloride and infuse over at least 30 minutes. Subcut: press on the site for 1–2 minutes.
claims.source_text: following desmopressin administration Dose: 0.3 microgram/kg (max 20 micrograms) stat intravenous infusion or subcutaneous administration Intravenous infusion: dilute to a final volume of 50 mL with Sodium Chloride 0.9% and infuse over at least 30 minutes Subcutaneous injection: apply pressure to the site for 1 to 2 minutes post injection
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'von Willebrand disease' (Last Updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/von_Willebrand_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Give clotting factor replacement immediately for severe or life-threatening bleeding.** Biostate (plasma-derived VWF/FVIII) may be needed in Type 1 with severe bleeding or DDAVP failure, and treats bleeding in Types 2 and 3. **Recombinant FVIII contains no VWF.**
claims.source_text: Give clotting factor replacement immediately if severe or life-threatening bleeding … Von Willebrand Factor/Factor VIII Plasma Concentrate (Biostate®) May be required in Type 1 VWD if severe bleeding or unresponsive to DDAVP Used to treat bleeding in people with Type 2 and Type 3 VWD A human plasma-derived product … Recombinant FVIII products do not contain von Willebrand factor
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'von Willebrand disease' (Last Updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/von_Willebrand_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Prescribe Biostate in Factor VIII units**, rounded to the closest vial size.
claims.source_text: prescribe according to Factor VIII units (eg Biostate® 2000 Factor VIII units). Round dosage to the closest vial size.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'von Willebrand disease' (Last Updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/von_Willebrand_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Biostate dose by bleed:** oral mucosa/epistaxis/menorrhagia 25 FVIII units/kg (60 VWF units/kg) · GI bleed 40 FVIII units/kg (96 VWF units/kg) · joint/muscle 40 FVIII units/kg (96 VWF units/kg).
claims.source_text: Type of bleeding Dose of Biostate® Oral mucosa/epistaxis/menorrhagia 25 Factor VIII units/kg (and 60 VWF units/kg) GI bleed 40 Factor VIII units/kg (and 96 VWF units/kg) Joint/muscle 40 Factor VIII units/kg (and 96 VWF units/kg)
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'von Willebrand disease' (Last Updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/von_Willebrand_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **CNS bleed, trauma or surgery: Biostate 60 FVIII units/kg (144 VWF units/kg).**
claims.source_text: Type of bleeding Dose of Biostate® … CNS bleed 60 Factor VIII units/kg (and 144 VWF units/kg) Trauma or surgery 60 Factor VIII units/kg (and 144 VWF units/kg)
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'von Willebrand disease' (Last Updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/von_Willebrand_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **No aspirin or NSAIDs** (e.g. ibuprofen, naproxen, diclofenac) — they may worsen bleeding.
claims.source_text: Do not use products containing aspirin or NSAIDs (eg ibuprofen, naproxen, diclofenac) as they may worsen bleeding
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'von Willebrand disease' (Last Updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/von_Willebrand_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Consider transfer for:** suspected intracranial haemorrhage · neck or throat bleeding · forearm or calf bleed risking compartment syndrome · hip or inguinal bleeding (iliopsoas risk) · undiagnosed abdominal pain · persistent haematuria · severe pain · **ongoing mucosal bleeding.**
claims.source_text: Any child with VWD and the following suspected intracranial haemorrhage bleeding into neck or throat forearm or calf bleed at risk of compartment syndrome bleeding into hip or inguinal area (due to risk of iliopsoas haemorrhage) undiagnosed abdominal pain persistent haematuria bleeding causing severe pain ongoing mucosal bleeding
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'von Willebrand disease' (Last Updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/von_Willebrand_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Discharge when** there is no active bleeding, follow-up is arranged and the family has a management plan (e.g. Haemophilia Treatment Centre Card).
claims.source_text: Consider discharge when No active bleeding Appropriate follow up is arranged Children are provided with a management plan eg Haemophilia Treatment Centre Card
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'von Willebrand disease' (Last Updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/von_Willebrand_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23
